children: Gold prices eased in early Asian trade on Wednesday, hitting their lowest in more than a year, weighed by a firmer US dollar and mounting expectations of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike next month, while investors awaited the Fed's October meeting minutes for fresh clues on the policy outlook.
FUNDAMENTALS
* Spot gold
fell 0.8% to $3,820.65 per ounce by 0036 GMT, hitting its lowest level since early October 2025. US gold futures
for December delivery slid 1.1% to $3,822.70.

* Gold sank to a one-year low on Monday, battered by a mix of high Treasury yields, a strong dollar and expectations of tighter monetary policy, putting bullion on course for further losses and its worst year in more than a decade.

* US retail sales increased moderately in October as households pulled back on purchases of motor vehicles and furniture, but maintained spending elsewhere, keeping the economy on solid footing at the start of the fourth quarter.

* The dollar fell from recent highs on Tuesday after mixed economic data showed steady consumer spending alongside a souring housing market, but the currency remained near its strongest level since April 2025.
* A stronger dollar makes greenback-priced bullion more expensive for buyers overseas.

* The US Federal Reserve may need several rate hikes to bring inflation under control and should act soon to ensure the problem does not get worse, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday.

* Fed Bank of New York President John Williams said on Tuesday the US central bank will likely need to raise rates again to lean against high inflation but he pushed back against the idea the Fed needs to shift to a more aggressive path of action.

* The US central bank should start preparing principles now for potential temporary and targeted interventions in the Treasury market in times of market stress that threatens to bleed over into the economy, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said on Tuesday.
* Markets see a 95.7% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point move is priced at 4.3%, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
* Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.
* Market participants await the minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, due later in the day, for further clues on the central bank's monetary policy trajectory.

* On the geopolitical front, the US and Iran exchanged fire on Tuesday, with the US striking an Iranian missile launch site after Iran said it targeted a US military radar system in Bahrain, despite talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar.
* Among other metals, spot silver
fell 0.9% to $46.97 per ounce, platinum
